the country in East Asia; in Zolai also called {Sen gam}
a Chinese-language daily newspaper of Malaysia, named as the source of news reports
<China> with the plural <te> written as one word: China as a body, its government, its companies or its people
the Chinese quarter of a city, as in Kuala Lumpur and San Francisco

of China or its people, the English word; {Chinese te} is the Chinese

name of a bus line that runs between Kalay and Yangon in Myanmar; from the Burmese name of the Chin Hills

the English form of the title of Jesus, used beside the Zolai <Khrih>

<Christian> and <biakna>, religion: the Christian religion, Christianity
the English word Christian with <upna>, faith: the Christian faith, Christianity as a religion; {i Christian upna} is our Christian faith
the Christians, followers of Christ
the Christian festival of the birth of Jesus, kept on 25 December

town and district in the south of Manipur, India, home of many Zomi; the town is also called Lamka
say as an order; <ci-in> after the quoted words reports the command that was given
say; stands after the words quoted, as in {a ci hi}, he said, and <ci-in>, saying
postpositional marker to indicate objective case
{Ci}, salt, written with a capital in place names: {Ci Tuipi} is the Salt Sea or Dead Sea, {Ci Kuam} the Valley of Salt and {Ci Khuapi} the City of Salt.

{ci ing}, the verb <ci> with the first person ending <ing>, written short with an apostrophe as is done in songs, where the count of words is fixed; the page gives {ci ing e} and {ci'ng e} as the same
<ci>, say, with the ending <in>: stands after quoted words and links them to what follows, saying so, with these words

terms: as big as/the size of/as much as
definition: Placed after a thing to give size or extent by comparison, as in {khut peek cia}, a handbreadth wide; {bang cia-in} asks how big.
sentence-final word of colloquial speech that gives a statement emphasis or feeling, often followed by <maw>; not the {cia} of size, which follows a noun

terms: as big as/the size of/about the size of
definition: <cia>, as big as, said twice and placed after a thing or a measure: of just that size, each about that big; {mihing ciacia} is life-size
go back to one's home or to the place one came from

terms: coming and going/going out and coming home
definition: <ciah>, go home, <leh>, and, and <kuan.1>, go out: every going out and coming home, all the daily movements of a person; stands before a verb such as <kidawp>, take care, to say wherever one goes; not <kuan.2>, who
<ciah>, go home, said twice for an action that goes on; the book uses it for the perfect continuous tense, {ka na ciahciah khinzo tading hi}, I will have been going home
<ciah> and <ding> written as one word: to go home, about to return

terms: in order to return/to go home
definition: <ciah>, return, and <dingin>, in order to, written as one word: so as to go back or go home

terms: when about to go home/when leaving
definition: <ciahding>, about to go home, and <teh>, when, written as one word: at the time of going back
{Ciah}, return, with <hak>, slow or late: be a long time in coming back.
<ciah> and <hun> written as one word: the time of going home, as in <vai ciahhun> and <sawm ciahhun>
{Ciah}, return or go home, with the linking ending <in>: returned and then did the next thing.
{Ciah}, return, with <khawm>, together: go back together with others.
{Ciah}, go home or return, with <khia>, out: go out and away from a place.
{Ciahkhia}, leave, with the causative <sak>: let or make someone go on his way.
Form of <ciahkhia>, leave, used before <ding>, <ciangin> and <khit>.
<ciahkhiat>, leave, and <ding> written as one word: to leave or go away from a country or place, mostly of what is ordered, allowed or forbidden

terms: be able to leave/can go home
definition: <ciahkhia>, leave, and <thei>, able, written as one word: be able or be allowed to leave a place
<ciahkhiat>, leave, with <pih>, together with: leave a place taking someone or something along
{Ciah}, return, with <khin>, already done: have gone back.
{Ciah}, return, with <kik>, back or again: go or come back to where one was.
<ciahkik>, return, and <ding>, the marker of what is to come, written as one word: will go back, or to go back
{Ciahkik}, return, with the linking ending <in> that joins it to the next action: returned and then.
<ciahkik>, return, and <leh>, if, written as one word: if one goes back
<ciahkik>, return, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not go or come back home
{Ciahkik}, return, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of going or coming back.
<ciahkik> and <nading> written as one word: for going back, in order to return
{Ciahkik}, return, with the causative <sak>: send someone back or let him go back.
{Ciahkik}, return, with the causative <sak> and the linking ending <in>: allowing someone to go back.
{Ciahkik}, return, with the plural <te>: the people who came back, said of the exiles who returned from Babylon.
<ciah>, go home, and <kuan.3>, about to, written as one word: at the point of leaving for home
Saying: roasting taro just when it is time to go home; the book lists it among its idiomatic expressions without explaining it, apparently said of starting a thing too late or at the wrong moment
<ciah> and <lam> written as one word: the way home, and after <hong> on the way back from a place
<ciah>, go home, and <leh>, if or when, written as one word
<ciah> and <lo> written as one word: not go back home
<ciah>, go home, with the noun suffix {-na}: the going home or the way home; paired with <hawhna> or <kuanna> for going out and coming back

terms: day of return/day of going home
definition: <ciah>, go home, and <ni>, day, written as one word: the day on which someone goes back; {vanah ciahni} is the day of going home to heaven, the day of death

terms: one who has returned/one who has come back
definition: {Ciah}, return, with <pa>, the man who does it: the man who has come back.
{Ciah}, go home, with <pah>, at once: go home straight away.
{Ciahpah}, go home at once, with the linking ending <in> that joins it to the next action.
{Ciah}, go home, with <pih>, together with: take or bring someone or something along to one’s home or back to a place.
<ciahpih>, take home, and <ding>, will, written as one word: will take or is to take someone or something home
{Ciahpih}, take home with one, with the linking ending <in>; another verb follows.
{Ciahpih}, take along home, with <kik>, back: bring or take someone or something back.
{Ciahpih}, take back with one, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of taking someone away to one’s own place.

terms: things brought home/what is brought in
definition: <ciahpih>, bring home, with the plural <te>: the things one has brought back
<ciahpih>, bring back, with <to>, upward, and the suffix <in>
{Ciah}, go home, with the causative <sak>: let or make someone go home; followed by <kik>, send back.
{Ciahsak}, send away, with the linking ending <in> that joins it to the next action.
{Ciahsak}, send home, with <kik>, back or again: send someone back or let him return.
{Ciahsak}, send away, with the noun suffix <na>: the sending away of someone, in Isaiah 50.1 of a wife sent away in divorce.

terms: plan to send back/intend to send home
definition: <ciahsak>, send home, with <sawm>, intend, written as one word: intend to send people back
{Ciah}, go home, with <san>, away from: go off and leave someone behind.

terms: go straight back/return directly/go home for good
definition: <ciah> and <suak> written as one word: return and carry right on, go straight home or back without stopping
{Ciah}, return, with <suak>, straight through, and <pah>, at once: go straight home without stopping.
{Ciah}, go home or return, with <suk>, downward: go down to one’s home.
<ciah>, go home, and <ta>, now or already, written as one word
<ciah>, go home, and the plural <te>, written as one word: the people who come or go back home, as in {gamdang pan hong ciahte}, those who came home from abroad

terms: be able to return/can go home
definition: <ciah>, return or go home, and <thei>, able, written as one word

terms: be able to return/can go home
definition: <ciah>, go home, and <theih>, can, written as one word; before <nading>, so that one can go home

terms: can still return/can still go home
definition: <ciahthei> and <lai> written as one word: still able to return

terms: go up home/go back up/come up
definition: {Ciah}, return, with <to>, upward: return or go home to a higher place.
<ciah>, return, and <toh>, upward, written as one word: go back up to a higher place, as home to the hills; the form of <ciahto> used before a following word
<ciah>, return, with <zawh>, after finishing: in the verse, counting days from when they had gone
sentence-final expression of colloquial speech, from <ci>, say: it adds feeling to a statement or a remark, much like indeed or I must say
placed after a verb of sounding such as <ham> or <khuang>: with a shrill sound that goes on and on, of insects humming or singing
Make the low rough sound of lion cubs.
of people, or of fowl, make a loud confused noise together, shouting, complaining or playing; often {ciak ngeingai}; the other sense is the growl of an animal
talk on and on, said of fools who multiply words
Said of those who came back from captivity; apparently another spelling or a misprint of <ciahkik>.
<ciak> with the expressive word <ngeingai>, written as one word: many people talking loudly at once, in merriment or in heated comment and argument
Engage someone to work or to fight for pay.
One step of a stairway, {kahlei cial}, or one level of a building.
ask someone to come, to take part or to do something, with no thought of pay, as a singer to sing or a guest to visit; in appeals {kong cial uh hi}, we call on you
poetic word for <dolcial>, used in songs; the book gives only this equivalent
{Cial}, hire, with the linking ending <in>: hiring someone and then going on to the next action.
{Cial}, hire, with the noun suffix <na>: the hiring of people, or what is spent to hire them.
a public invitation or appeal asking people to come, pray or take part, not hiring for pay; {cialna nei} is make an appeal
{Cial}, hire, with <pa>, the man who does it: the one who hires or sends a worker.
a large series of Christian meetings held to preach salvation and renew the churches; <cialpi bawl> is hold a crusade

terms: hold a crusade/hold a revival meeting
definition: <cialpi>, crusade, and <bawl>, make: hold a series of evangelistic or revival meetings; the place stands before it with <ah>
plural of <cialpi>: the evangelistic meetings of a preacher
<cial>, hire, with <sawm>, intend, written as one word: be looking to hire someone for pay
<cial>, ask someone to do a thing, with <sawn>, on to another: pass a task on by asking someone else to do it
{Cial}, hire, with the plural <te>: those who are hired; {galkap cialte} are mercenaries.
Plural of <cial>, step or level: the floors of a building.
Give one’s word or swear an oath; often with <thu>, as in {thu ciam}, make a promise on oath
Try a little food or drink.
{Ciam}, promise or swear, with the linking ending <in>; often after <thu> or <kam>.
{Ciam}, taste, with the linking ending <in>.
{Ciam}, taste, with <kha>, which shows that the action comes to happen: get to taste.
{Ciam}, promise, with <kha>: happen to give one’s word, as in {kam ciamkha}.
{Ciam}, promise, with <khawm>, together: join with others in making a promise.
{Ciam}, promise, with <kholh>, beforehand; {a ciamkholh ni} is the appointed day.
{Ciam} with the noun suffix <na>: what someone has promised or sworn.
In {sih ciamna}, a will that takes effect at death.
{Ciam}, promise, with <na> and <sa>, already done: describes what has been promised, here the place the Lord promised.
Speak in fun and not seriously; compare <ciamnuih>, jest.
Mockery or joking at someone’s expense: {ciamnuih bawl} is mock or make fun of someone, {ciamnuih-a neih} is treat as a laughingstock.
used as a verb, with the prefix <ki> as {ki ciamnuih}: joke with one another in fun
<ciamnuih>, a jest, and <bawlna>, doing: joking or mockery, the noun of {ciamnuih bawl}; {ciamnuih bawlna in nei} is to treat a thing or a person as a joke
Saying: a joke turns into a fight; said when what began as fun or teasing ends in a real quarrel; the book lists it among its idiomatic expressions without explaining it
{Ciamnuih}, mockery, with <bawl>, make: make fun of someone.
<ciamnuih>, joke, and the verb particle <kha> written as one word: happen to say something as a joke
A person or people that others make fun of.
Something said or done in fun: {ka ciamnuihna hi} is I was only joking.
{Ciam}, promise, with <pa>, the man who does it: he who made the promise, said of God.
{Ciam}, promise or vow, with <pak>, quickly: make a vow in haste.
<ciam>, promise, and <peello>, without fail, written as one word: not breaking what was promised or fixed, every time as expected
The pin of a loom, with which the woven cloth is beaten tight.

terms: break one's word/break a promise/go back on an oath
definition: {Ciam}, promise, with <pel>, miss: fail to keep a promise; mostly negated, as in {ciampel lo}, keep one’s word.
{Ciampel}, break a promise, with the linking ending <in>; in a list of faults, treacherous.
<ciampel>, break a promise, with the noun suffix <na>
{Ciam} with <sa> for a completed act: already promised; {na ciamsa bangin} is as you promised.
<ciam>, taste, with the causative <sak>: let someone taste food or drink, and so let someone come to know a thing by trying it
A curse, or an oath that brings harm; {ciamsiatna ngah} is be cursed.
{ciamsiat}, curse, with <sa>, already done: that has been cursed
Take note of something, keep it in mind or put it on record.
<ciamteh>, note or mark, and the future marker <ding> written as one word: will mark or regard, to be noted
{Ciamteh}, note or record, with the linking ending <in> that joins it to the next verb, often <gelh>, write.
<ciamteh>, record, and <khat>, one, written as one word; after <aki> it means one that is recorded or regarded as what is named before it
<ciamteh> and <lai>, still, written as one word; {ki ciamtehlai} is it is still recorded or regarded as

Plural of <ciamtehna>: the seals on a scroll, marks borne on the body, signs set up on a road.
plural of <ciamtehna>: things noted down and kept
{Ciamteh}, note or consider, with <pa>, the one who does it: said of God, who counts things not yet existing as existing.
<ciamteh> and <pah> written as one word: take note of something at once; with <ki>, be noted or remembered straight away
<ciamteh>, record, and <phot>, for the time being, written as one word: put on record as such for now, until more is known
{Ciamteh}, mark, with <sa> for a completed act: already marked out.
{Ciamteh}, mark or record, with <sak>: put a mark on someone, or hold a sin on record against someone.
<ciamteh>, record or mark, with <ta>, marking a change that has now come about, written as one word
{Ciamteh}, note or record, with the last syllable repeated for continued action: go on holding in mind.
<ciam>, promise, with <zah>, amount
{Ciam}, swear, with <zo>, done and settled; <thu> or <kam> stands before it.
Pile up a heap or build up a wall; written with a final apostrophe in the text.
Stands after a verb of looking, thinking or knowing: closely and thoroughly.
be left over or still there after the rest is gone, often with <lai>, still, or <nawnlo>, no longer; not the adverb that follows a verb of knowing or saying
poetic word for <dak>, the gong, used in songs
Marks the point reached in place or time, often followed by <dong>.
At the time that; a short form of <ciangin>.
{Ciang}, rod, written with a capital; {ukna ciang} is the scepter of a ruler.

<ciang> with <a>, joining a time clause to the words that follow: when; <khit cianga> means after
<ciang> with the marker <a> written <aa>, used like <ciangin>: when, at the time that, after
<ciang> with the place marker <ah>: at or up to the point named, in place or extent
<ciang>, up to, and <bang>, about, written as one word after a number or amount: roughly that much, up to about

terms: only up to/only as far as
definition: <ciang>, up to, with <bek>, only: no further than the number or point named
<ciang> in its meaning when, with <bek>, only: not until that has happened, mostly as {tua ciangbek}, only then, where the other sense sets a limit that is not passed
<ciangbek>, only up to, and <hilo>, is not: placed after a word or clause and mostly followed by <in>, not only that much; the next clause adds what goes beyond it
<ciangbek>, only then, with <in>, written as one word: not before the time or event named

terms: as far as/up to/to the full extent
definition: doubled <ciang>, every point reached: {tu ciangciang} is thus far, {zah ciangciang} is as much as, and {a ciangciang-ah} is on every side
<ciangciang> and <ah> written as one word: as far as a point reaches; {tu ciangciangah} is up to now, {abei sa ciangciangah} in time past, and after a verb as far as one can
<ciangciang> and <in> written as one word: right up to a day or point; {tu ni ciangciangin} is up to today, and {a ciangciangin} is by its levels or bounds
<ciang> and <dong> written as one word after a time, a place or a clause: right up to that point
a rod or stick used for beating as punishment
after <nung> or <khit>: {a nung ciangin} is afterwards, later on
after <tua>, that: {tua ciangin} is then or and then, the usual way to begin the next step of a story
joins a clause to what follows: when or after this happened, and then
text: as in Let there be light, and there was light"

definition: placed after a word of time such as <hun>, <ni> or <kum> to say when something happens: at that time, on that day, in or by that year
the two words <ciangin>, when or after, and <leitungah>, on the earth, printed as one word
<ciangin>, when, and <zong>, also, written as one word: even when, also at the time when; after a day or time, on that day too
a narrow way through hills or into a place
<ciangka> written with a capital: the narrow way through the hills at Mikmash
a plain stick or dry rod
plural of <ciangkang>; the rods, peeled to show white, that Jacob set before the flocks
plural; apparently <ciang>, stick, with <khai>, hang: a load carried on a pole, where the English has basket

terms: to some extent/to a certain degree
definition: <ciang>, as far as, and <khat>, one, written as one word: up to a certain point, to some extent; the same letters can also be {ciang khat}, one stick
a stick carried in the hand: a walking staff, a shepherd’s rod or a ruler’s scepter
<ciangkhut>, staff, with the place marker <ah>; {ciangkhutah sik phuh}, fix an iron point on a goad
<ciangkhut>, staff or rod, with the suffix <in>
plural of <ciangkhut>, staff or rod
build up again a wall that is broken, from <ciang>, build a wall, and <kik>, again
<ciang> and <leh> written as one word: when, at the time that, joining the clause to what follows

<ciang>, as far as, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word after a noun in {-na}: the point that has been reached, what something has come to, as the topic of the sentence; {tuni i hihna ciangpen} is what we are as of today
<ciang>, build up a wall, with <pha>, good: repair a broken wall and make it sound again
a large basket; in the vision of Zechariah 5 the ephah measuring basket
a stick used for beating
a fixed limit, especially of time; {hun ciangtan} is an appointed length of time
fix the measure or limit of a thing, such as the length of a life or a ration of food
<ciangtan>, a limit, and <omlo>, there is none: with no limit set, of time, amount or power; mostly with <in> before a verb, and {ahun ciangtan omlo in} is for an indefinite time
<ciangtan>, set a limit, and <ding> written as one word: to limit, or the limiting of, a power or a number
in {siam ciangtang}, the shuttle of a weaver's loom
set a limit or a fixed measure for something; with <ki>, be limited or fixed; the noun is written <ciangtan>
<ciangtan>, set a limit, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not limited; {kum ciangtanlo} is without limit of age
<ciangtan>, set a limit, with the noun suffix <na>: a limit that is set, a restriction; {ciangtanna omlo in} is without limit
<ciangtan>, set a limit, with <sa> marking a finished action: that has been limited or fixed beforehand, as a day or an amount
<ciangtan> and <sak> written as one word: fix the limit or measure of a thing for someone
<ciangtan>, set a limit, and <zah>, amount, written as one word: the amount that has been fixed, as in {aki ciangtanzah sangin}, more than the amount laid down
<ciang>, here stick or rod, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with a stick, as in {ciangtawh sat}, beat with a stick

terms: to the extent of/as far as
definition: <ciang>, as far as, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a phrase: with as much as that, to that extent
a long piece of wood held in the hand, used to strike, push or lever
those who build up a wall, apparently <cian> build up with the plural <te>; {kulh ciangte} is the builders of the wall
<ciang> build a wall, with <to> upward: build a wall up high
postpositional marker indicating its been done
of a wall; apparently <cian>, build up, with <zo>, be able, and not the word <ciang>, until
<ciang>, when, with <zong>, also, written as one word after a clause: when that happens too, even when
<ciang>, stick, with <zum>, pointed: the pointed stick used to drive oxen
the second part of {ki cianin}, <kician> with <in> divided otherwise: exactly, clearly, in a proper form; once it is a spelling of <ciangin>
still be there after the rest is gone or done; {a cianlai} is the rest, those who remain
<cian> build up with the noun suffix <na>; {kulh cianna} is the building of the wall

<cian>, clearly and thoroughly, with the noun suffix <na>, after a verb of saying, asking or looking: the doing of it clearly and in full, {gen cianna} an exact statement, {hilh cianna} a clear explanation, {et cianna} a close examination; not the building of a wall
<cian>, pile up, with <pi>, great: a great heap of stones raised against a city wall
<cian>, clearly, with the causative <sak>: make something clear; {kilang ciansak} is make something show clearly
<cian>, remain, and <ta> written as one word: only this much is now left
<cian>, clear and definite as in <kician>, with <tak>; mostly followed by <in> and also written {ki ciantak in}: clearly, exactly, with certainty
<cian> carefully or clearly, with <takin> which makes an adverb
try the taste of food or drink
only in {ciap teh}, the two-word spelling of <ciapteh>, take note of or keep in mind, and in {ciap tehna}, a record or recognition; not {ciap}, taste
<ciap>, form of <ciam>, taste, with <khit>, after finishing
<ciap> taste, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of tasting
<ciapteh>, note down or mark, and <ding>, will, written as one word: something to take note of, to be recorded or set
heading of a remark that the reader should take note of, shortened to <ctd>
<ciamteh>, mark, note, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: noteworthy
a mark or seal put on a thing or a person to show whose it is
text: as in put a mark on objects

definition: what is written down to be kept or remembered, a record or note, and the standing that is so recorded, as in {ciaptehna ngah}, be put on record as; not a mark or seal on a thing
plural of <ciaptehna>: marks or signs put on something, and things written down as a record
<ciapteh>, note or record, with <sak>, for another or cause: put something on record for someone, register a person as something, or have it recorded
<ciapteh>, take note, with <tak>, here worthy of: deserving to be noted or kept in mind

terms: be able to recognise/be able to register
definition: <ciapteh> and <theih> written as one word, the form before <nading>: be able to record or recognise a person as something

terms: fit to be noted/that ought to be recorded
definition: <ciamteh>, mark, note, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to be noted
placed after a noun or verb to show that it applies to each one separately
to or in each one's own, placed after a noun of place
doubled <ciat>, each: each one’s own, said of every kind or every land separately
placed after a verb, or a noun such as <mihing>, like single <ciat>: every one does the thing, each for himself, where the Bible sense is each one’s own kind or land

terms: to its kind/each according to its kind
definition: <ciatciat> with the ending <in>, after <nam>, kind: each according to its own kind
<ciatciat> with the noun suffix {-na}, after a verb: the doing of it steadily, one after another; the exact sense is uncertain
<ciat> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: each one should or will do it
<ciat>, each, with the ending <in>: each one separately, as in {min ciatin}, each by name
after <nam>, kind, or <beh>, clan: each according to its own
<ciat>, each, with the noun suffix <na>, placed after a verb: the fact or the way of each one doing it
<ciat>, each, and the verb ending {-ni}, let us, written as one word after a verb: let each of us do it
<ciat>, each, and <pan.1>, from, written as one word after a noun: from each of them, each from its own
<ciat>, each, and the particle <ta> written as one word, placed after a verb in a wish or request, before <hen> or <un>: may each one, let each one
<ciat> each, with the plural ending <te>: each one of several
<ciat>, each, with the plural ending <un>: each of them in his own way
poetic word for <gun>, used in songs
the river on the border between Chin State in Myanmar and Mizoram in India, and the border crossing near Rih that is reached by the road from Tedim
placed after a verb: the action is done in small repeated bits and keeps on, as birds chirping, an animal nibbling or money saved a little at a time
<ci>, say, with <bang>, like, written as one word: of the kind just named, and the like; {bang cibang} is how, in what way, and {tua cibang in} is in that way
<cibang> with the linking ending {-a} before a noun: {hih cibanga}, of this kind
after <bang>, what: {bang cibangin} asks in what manner an action is done, the question an adverb of manner answers; also written as one word, <bangcibangin>
<cibang>, of that kind, with the plural ending: things of the kind just described, as in {hih cibangte}, such as these
a lump or swelling that forms on or in the body
<ci>, say, and <bilbel> written as one word, closing a news report: it is said that, as it turned out, mostly of harm that did not happen

terms: say after all/as the saying goes
definition: <ci>, say, and the particle <buang> written as one word after quoted words, mostly as {cibuang hiven}: as they do say, as the saying goes
reduplicated <ci> say; {hong cici kei in} is do not keep telling me
<ci>, say, with an expressive ending, closing a sentence that reports what someone says or what is being told; the exact shade of the ending is not certain
in good health; {cidam lo} is sick
<cidam>, healthy, with the linking ending {-a}: in good health, being well, said before the verb
<cidam>, healthy, with <huailo>, not fit to, written as one word: not good for health, unwholesome
<cidam>, healthy, with the ending <in>: in good health, unharmed
<cidam>, healthy, with <kik>, again; with <sak>, restore to health
<cidam>, healthy, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not in good health; {lungsim cidamlo} is mentally ill
<cidam>, healthy, and <lohna>, the state of not being, written as one word: the state of not being well
<cidamlo>, unwell, with the plural ending <te>: people who are not in good health
<cidam>, healthy, with <mel>, look: appear to be in good health; the book gives <mel> as the word that completes the meaning
noun from <cidam> be healthy; {cidamna ngah} is to be healed
<cidamna>, health, with <lamsang>, side: the health side of public life, the health sector; with <ah>, in the field of health, and before a noun, health as in health work or health benefit

terms: for health/in order to be healthy
definition: <cidam>, healthy, and <nading>, for, written as one word: for the sake of health, so as to be well
causative of <cidam>, healthy
<cidamsak>, make healthy, with the suffix <in>
<cidamsak>, make healthy, with <kik>, again
<cidam> healthy with <suak> become; here a command, be well
<cidam>, healthy, and <tak> written as one word, usually followed by <in>: in good health, safe and sound
<cidam> with the plural <te>: those that are healthy, said of people, animals and sound trees
<cidam>, healthy, with <zaw>, more
<ci> and <dan>, way, written as one word: the way something is or is done; {bang cidan} is how, of what kind, and {hih cidan in} is in this way
<ci>, salt, with <dat>, substance: salt as a substance in food or in the body; also written beside the word iodine
<ci>, say, and <den>, always, written as one word: say again and again or as a habit
<ci>, say, with <ding>, will, written as one word: will say, is to say; in a question, shall one say
a cigarette; also explained as <zatep>
postpositional marker to indicate objective case
placed after a statement it marks it as what is said, heard or known, as in {cih kiza hi}, it is heard that, and {cih thu}, the news that

terms: it was found that/it turned out that/it was discovered that
definition: <cih>, the marker that closes what is said, and <kimukhia>, be found out: placed after a whole clause and before the final <hi>, it presents the clause as what an inquiry, a test or a count has brought to light

terms: it is reported that/it is said that
definition: <cih>, the marker that closes what is said, and <kiza>, be heard: placed after a whole clause and before the final <hi>, it presents the clause as news that is heard and not confirmed by the writer

<cih>, saying, and <thadah>, lazy, literally too lazy to say: placed after a word or clause, it sets that aside as out of the question and the clause that follows, often with <nangawn>, even, names the lesser thing that is the case

<cih>, that or called, <thulu>, title, and <tawh>, with: placed after the quoted title or theme of a writing, sermon, song or statement and before the verb of writing, speaking or publishing, it says that the work bears that title
<cih> and <bang> written as one word: after a word or a list, such a thing as, things like; after a verb of saying with its subject, as was said

terms: there is no such thing as/nothing like
definition: <cihbang>, things like, and <omlo>, there is not: placed after a word or a clause and before <hi>, denies that anything of the kind exists
<cih>, say, and <bangbang>, whatever, written as one word: whatever someone says, exactly as someone says, after the one who speaks; {a cihbangbang} is whatever he says
<cihbang> and <bek> written as one word, after a number or a list: only such as these, no more than that
<cihbang>, such as, with <bel>, as for, written as one word after a word or clause and before a negative: as for anything like that, there is none

terms: such as/in the manner of/things like
definition: <cih>, <bang> and <dan> written as one word, placed after quoted words or a list: in that kind of way, things of that sort

terms: as said/according to what is said
definition: <cih>, say, with <bangin>, as, written as one word; {na cihbangin}, as you say
placed after a list of names, numbers or examples, which are only samples of what the sentence goes on to say: in such ways as these
<cihbang> and <peuh> written as one word after a list: any such things as these, whatever is of that kind

terms: with such things as/and the like
definition: <cihbang>, such as, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a list: with things like these, in such ways
<cih> and <bangte> written as one word, placed after a list: things such as these, and the like

terms: all such as/and the like/and so on
definition: <cihbang>, such as, and <teng>, here all of them, written as one word after a list: all the things just named and those like them

terms: such things as also/even the like
definition: <cihbang>, such as, and <zong>, also, written as one word: after a word or a list, things like these too, or not even such a thing
<cih>, saying, and <bek>, only, written as one word after a quoted word or statement: only that and nothing more is said, known or written
<cihbek> and <tawh.2> written as one word after a name or word: with only that much said, named or written only so

<cih>, saying or that, and the particle <bel>, here as for, written as one word: placed after a word or clause to make it the topic, as for whether or as for what is called, mostly before a negative statement

terms: as for what is called/only that much
definition: <cih> and <ciang> written as one word. After a word or statement, {cihciang in} takes it up as the topic: when one says this, what is meant by it. With <bek> or alone before a verb of knowing or hearing it limits what is known: only this much, no more than that

<cihciang>, as far as what is called, and <bektawh>, with only: placed after a name or a description in a news report, it says that the person is made known by that much alone and no further name or detail is given; a verb such as <kipulak>, be announced, follows
<cih>, saying, with <ciangbek>, only as far as, written as one word: placed after a name or word to show that no more than this is said or known
<cih> and <ciangin> written as one word: when one says, used to take up a word or statement and then explain what it means
<cih>, form of <ci> say, doubled to show repeated or continued saying
<cihcih> and <te> written as one word: the things people keep saying or calling so; {i cihcihte} is the things we speak of, what we call

terms: as if to say/in the manner of saying
definition: <cih>, saying, and <daan>, manner, written as one word, placed after a quoted statement: in the way of saying that, something like, as if to say

terms: such as/and the like/that sort of
definition: <cih>, saying, and <dan>, manner, written as one word after a list, an example or a quoted thought: things such as these, the kind of thing just said; {cihdan in} is in such a way

terms: in the manner of/as if to say
definition: <cihdan> and <in> written as one word, after a quoted thought or an example: in such a way, as if saying so
<cihdan>, such as, with the plural <te> written as one word after a list or a quoted saying: things of that kind
<cih> and <ding> written as one word: that is to be said or called, what one may say; <cihding ahihi> is it must be said, one may say

terms: one may say/it must be said/so to speak
definition: <cihding>, to be said, and <ahihi>, it is: closes a sentence in which the writer gives a judgement or a name for what was told, one has to call it that; the judgement stands before it, as in {phadawm cihding ahihi}, it must be called fortunate

terms: even to/down to/to the point of
definition: <cih>, saying, and <dong>, until, written as one word after a clause or a list: up to and including what was just named, to the extent of saying so; followed by <in> or <ah>
<cih> and <hang> written as one word, after a statement: because it is said to be so, merely on the ground that; with <in> also although it is said that
<cih>, saying, and <hangin>, although, written as one word after a statement: although it is said to be so, even so
<cih> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a statement: so it is said, so he or she said; the same as {ci hi}
<cih> and <huai> written as one word: it deserves to be said; after a question ending in <hiam> it means one cannot help wondering whether
<cih> and <hun>, time, written as one word after a phrase: the time of that, times such as that
<ci>, say, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word; in news reports it closes a statement that is passed on from others: it is said
<ci>, say, with <hiau>, a word that shows a quick and direct action, written as one word after the words quoted: say straight out or all at once
<cih> with the suffix {-in}; in the formula {kong cihin ah}, I say to you, introducing a statement
of a fire; {mei cih}, light a fire
<cihin> with <ah>, in the formula {kong cihinah}, I say to you, introducing a statement
<cih> and <kammal>, word, written as one word after a word that is quoted: the word so called, the term
<cih> and <kawmkal> written as one word and followed by <ah>: while it was so, in the midst of what the clause before it says
<cih> do or say, with <kha> happen to: used with <bang> or <bangmah>, do something to someone, usually harm
<cih>, say, with <khak>, form of <kha>, happen to: of something one fears others may say
<cih> and <khat> written as one word, placed after a name or a quoted saying: a thing or person that is called so
<cih> and <khawng> written as one word, placed after one or more examples: things like that, and so on

terms: as for such things as/things like
definition: <cihkhawng>, and the like, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word, after one or more examples: as for things like these

terms: such things as/and the like also
definition: <cih>, <khawng> and <zong> written as one word after a statement: things such as this also, there are even cases like this
<cih>, form of <ci>, say, with <khit>, finish; before <ciangin> or <phetin>: after or as soon as someone has said; in Acts 10:16 of a thing having been done
<cih>, say, and <kik>, again, written as one word: say the same thing again
<cih> and <la>, song, written as one word, placed after the title or the first words of a song: the song called so, the song that says so
<cih>, that or such as, and the emphatic <lah>, written as one word before a negative: not even that, nothing like; {gim cihlah nei lo} is having no such thing as tiredness
<cih>, say, and <lai> in the sense still, written as one word: still saying, go on saying for the time being

terms: the sense that/to the effect that
definition: <cih> and <lam> written as one word after a quoted thought: the direction or sense of saying so, to the effect that
<cih> and <leh> written as one word: if one says or asks; {banghang hiam cihleh} is if one asks why, that is, because
<cih>, the form of the verb say or do, with <lo>, not, written as one word; {bangmah cihlo} is said or did nothing, did not respond, did no harm to
<cih> and <loh> written as one word, not saying: placed after a noun, apart from that one; often followed by {a dang om kei}, there is no other
<cih>, saying, and the emphatic <mah> written as one word: the very thing that is said; {a cihmah bangin} is just as he said

terms: be in distress/be desperate/be in trouble
definition: be at a loss what to do; also used as a noun for distress or heartache
state of being helpless and in want
plural of <cihmawhna> distress or need
<cih> say, with <mawk> carelessly or without ground: say something that does not hold, as in even if it should say
after a name or a figure and before the topic marker <pen>, {cihmawk} points to the thing just named, what is called, and carries no idea of careless speech: {NATO cihmawk pen} is what is called NATO
apparently <cih>, say, with <mel>, appearance: {thutang cihmel thei lo}, not know what justice is; exact sense not confirmed
what someone says or means, noun form of <cih> say
what a thing is called or means; after a name, {a cihna} gives another name for the same place or person

terms: it means/that is to say/which means
definition: <cihna>, the saying or meaning, and <ahihi>, it is: placed at the end of a sentence after a statement, it presents that statement as the meaning or consequence of what was said before, it means that

terms: does not mean/it is not to say
definition: <cihna>, saying or meaning, and <hilo>, is not: placed after a whole statement and usually followed by <hi>, it denies that the statement is what is meant; {ka cihna hilo hi} is I do not mean
<cih>, here do, and <nading>, for, written as one word: what one should do; nearly always with <theilo>, not know what to do, be at a loss
<cih>, say, with <nak>, written as one word before <leh>: {na cihnak leh} is if you say, whenever you say
plural of <cihna>; placed after quoted words, these sayings
<cih> say with <nop> want, the form of <nuam> used in dependent clauses

terms: one feels like saying/it makes one want to say
definition: <cihnop>, want to say, with the suffix <huai>, causing that feeling: placed after a quoted remark or question, often with <mahmah> or <mawk>, the writer's way of adding a comment, one cannot help saying
<cihnop>, want to say, and <huai>, causing that feeling, written as one word: it makes one want to say, one could well say
what someone means or wants to say

terms: that is to say/in other words/what is meant is
definition: <cihnopna>, meaning, and <ah>, at: opens a sentence that explains what was just said, often closed by {cihna ahi hi}; with a possessive before it, {ka cihnopna ah} is what I mean is and {a cihnopna ah} is what he means is
the man of whom something is said, <cih>, say, with <pa> marking a man
<cih> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word, placed after a word or phrase to make it the subject spoken about: what is called, the thing named
<cih> and <peuh> written as one word, placed after a word or clause: anything of that name, any such thing as that
<cih> and <peuhmah> written as one word after a noun or phrase, mostly before a negative: anything that could be called that, no such thing at all
<cih> and <phial> written as one word, mostly as {cihphial ding}: one could almost say, practically
<cih>, say, with <pih>, together with or to someone: say a thing in agreement with another
what has already been said or proposed, <cih> with <sa> for a completed action; {na cihsa bangin}, as you have said
<cih> say with <sak>, done for another person: {va cihsak un} is go and say it for me; in Galatians 1:7, let a thing be called by a name
of a fire, light it for someone
<cih>, say, with a particle of emphasis, indeed or for our part, written as one word; {i cihsam hang} is although we do say so; the second part is not <sam>, call
<cih>, form of <ci> say, with <san>, at or toward someone: say something at a person, often to mock or to dismiss them
<cih>, saying, with the word for than, as in {cih sang in}, written as one word and often followed by <in>: rather than saying or being so, with <zaw> on the thing preferred
<cih>, that, with <sangin>, than, written as one word after a statement: rather than saying or asking that, usually followed by a clause with <zaw>
<cihsan>, say in reply, and <lel>, merely, written as one word at the end of a quoted remark: he just said, he simply answered
<cihsan>, say to or at someone, and <ziau>, lightly and at once, written as one word: just say it in reply, remark without more ado
apparently <cih>, say, with <taak>, worthy: be worth counting, of a small amount among many people
true and loyal to a person or to God; {cihtak loh} or {cihtak kei} is to be unfaithful, {cihtak lohna} is unfaithfulness
between a verb and its repetition, usually with <in>, it says that the action is done for real and to the full, as in {sim cihtak in ka sim} I read it in earnest; not about loyalty
placed between a repeated word, as {hai cihtakin hai}, to say that it is so in the full sense of the word
not being faithful, to God or to a spouse: <cihtak> faithful with <loh> not and {-na}
the quality of being faithful and true, <cihtak> with the noun suffix <na>; {cihtakna tawh} is faithfully
plural of <cihtakna>: the ways in which a person is faithful and true
<cihtak>, faithful, with <zawk>, more: surpass others in doing what is right

terms: with what is called/with the saying
definition: <cih> and <tawh> written as one word after quoted words or a clause: with what is said or named; {cihtawh kisai} is concerning the statement that

<cihtawh>, with what is called, and <thu.2>, a case: placed after the name of an offence or of a section of law and before <kibawl> or <bawl>, a case is opened under that name, the person is charged with it

terms: also as/also with what is called
definition: <cihtawh> and <zong>, also, written as one word after a name or a clause: also by that name, also on that account
said of firewood, <sing>: apparently get or use for oneself, with <tawm> marking an action done for oneself; the exact sense of <cih> here is not clear
plural of <cih>, placed after a list or a name: the things called, what is called
<cihte>, such things as, and <akipan>, beginning with: placed after one or more examples that have been named, beginning with these and going on to the rest of the same kind
<cihte>, those called, and <pawl>, group: placed after one example or a list of examples, things or people of that kind, the likes of these

terms: when one says/by this is meant
definition: <cih>, say, and <teh> written as one word after the word or statement that is explained, often with <ka> or <ih> before it: when one says this, what is meant by it is
<cih> and <teng>, here meaning all, written as one word, placed after a list: all these, all the things just named
<cihteng>, all these just named, and <bek>, only, written as one word after a list: only these and no others
<cihte>, such things as, and <pan>, from, written as one word after a list of names: from those named, from such as these

terms: such as/and the like/those of the kind
definition: <cihte> and <pawl> written as one word, placed after a name, a list or a quoted saying: those called so and others like them, people or things of that kind
<cihte> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word, placed after a list or a name: as for such things as these, as for what is called
<cihte> and <peuh> written as one word after a list: any such things as these, things like these
<cihte>, such things as, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a list: with these and the like

terms: and the like also/such things too
definition: <cihte>, such things as, and <zong>, also, written as one word after a list: these things too, things such as these as well
<cih> and <thadah> written as one word, a fixed expression after a phrase: let alone that, never mind that, what follows being a smaller thing that also fails
<cih> with <tham>, worth: worth saying; mostly with a negative, as {cihtham hetlo}, not worth mentioning, nothing by comparison

terms: be able to say/be able to do
definition: <cih>, say or do, with <thei>, can; with <bangmah> and a negative, be unable to say or do anything
apparently a form of <cithei> prosper; {a cihtheih pen hun} is the time when he is best off
<cih> say with <theih> can: it can be said; {cihtheih hi lo} is nothing can be said to him, he is past telling
state of being well off and at peace, the opposite of <cihmawhna>, need

<cih>, say, with <theih>, can, and the noun suffix <na>: that something can be said, or the reason why one can say it, {tua bang ka cihtheihna in} the reason I can say so is; not the state of being well off
<cih>, which closes what is said, and <thu>, word or matter, written as one word: the news, report or matter that something is so; {cihthu kiza hi} is it is reported that

terms: it is reported that/word has come that
definition: <cihthu>, the news that, and <kiza>, be heard: a news formula placed after a full statement and before <hi>, marking it as a report the writer has heard and not seen
<cih>, said, with <tuak> in its use for a supposition: it is probably as said, that must be it; the book quotes {tua cihtuak mah e}
<cih>, say, with <tuam>, separate: a setting apart; {cihtuam om loin} is without distinction, regardless of
<cih>, the form of <ci>, and the plural <uh> written as one word; {bang a cihuh} is what or how they did
<cih> and <vai> written as one word after a statement: the matter that, the question whether; usually followed by {tawh kisai}, concerning

terms: amount demanded/as much as one says
definition: <cih>, say, with <zah>, amount: whatever amount someone names
<cih>, do, with <zawh>, be able: be able to do something to; {bangmah a cihzawh kei leh} is if it can do nothing to it, if the thing is not harmed
<cih>, saying, with <ziau>: said simply or lightly, just putting it so
<cih>, do, with <zo>, be able: be able to do something to someone; {bang hong cihzo ding} is what can they do to me
<cih>, the word that closes what is said or thought, with <zong>, also, written as one word: that too, even the saying of it; {cihzong kiza hi} is it is also reported that

terms: it is also reported that/it is also said
definition: <cihzong>, also that, and <kiza>, be heard: closes a sentence of a news report, before <hi>, and marks its content as a further thing that is reported or heard, not seen by the writer
the seed of a plant, spelled with a long vowel in the book to keep it apart from <ci>, salt; {ankam cii} is mustard seed
placed after <mong>, end: the very end, the outermost edge
of speech, words or writing: deep and genuine, as the old people speak; after <pau> or <kam>, not after <mong> as in the sense of the farthest end
of wine, well aged and of the best kind

terms: first/at the very start/for the first time
definition: after a verb, the first time or the very moment something begins, not the aged wine of the other sense: {ka zak ciil} is when I first heard, and {a kipat ciil ni} is the day it first started
unwilling to give or share, the opposite of <cingh>, generous
Clear: of the eye, healthy and seeing well; of water, settled and clear.
of a person, having good sense and sound judgement, beyond schooling; mostly paired with <pil>, as {pil leh ciim}, wise and sensible
Wisdom or skill, a clear and discerning mind; <ciim> with the noun ending <na>.
old settlement in the Tedim area that Zomi tradition names as the place from which the clans spread; also used in the names of a magazine and a school
Saying: meat fed at Ciimnuai is repaid at Geltui; a kindness is never forgotten and is surely repaid some day
<ciim>, clear in mind, with the causative <sak>: make wise or discerning, as in {mi ciimsate ciimsak}, make those who are already wise still wiser
soak through, in {kawt ciimsak}, said of rain wetting people to the skin
<ciim>, here clear in mind or wise, with <sa> already and the plural <te>: people who are already wise
<ciim> with <tak>, which makes an adverb: with care and good sense, as in {piltak le ciimtak-in}, wisely and prudently; of sleep, {ihmut ciimtak in}, soundly, getting enough
place on the road to Tedim, eight or nine miles from the town, known for its ridge and its bends in the road
<ciim>, sensible, with the plural <te>: people of good sense and sound judgement
Plant or grow crops; written {ciin’} before a following word or suffix, as in {na ciin’te}, the things you plant.
said of rain, {guah ciin} is rain that goes on without stopping
<ci-in> written as one word, <ci>, say, with the ending {-in}: stands after quoted or reported words and before a verb of saying, asking or answering; not the verb plant
poetic word for <u>, used in songs

<ciin>, here keep or perform and not the particle saying, joined by <le> to <zuih>, follow or observe: a ritual, a fixed practice that is kept and followed, said of religious rites and of customs done for form. Stands as a noun, with <te> for the plural or <khat> for one
<ciin>, plant, with <dan>, way, written as one word: how a crop or a flower is planted and grown
the accepted way of behaving among a people, named beside <pau>, language, and <ngeina>, tradition
<ciin>, plant, and <ding>, the marker of what is to be done, written as one word: planting that is to be done
Unable to bear children; said of a woman, and also of animals.
plant and grow a crop in a field or garden, with the crop named before it, as in {buh ciing}, grow rice; another spelling of <ciin>, not the adjective barren
counting word for hill fields, placed before the number, as in {lo ciingnih ciingthum}, two or three fields or stretches of field; the size it names is not stated on the page
do to a person what he objects to, apparently make fun of him or ape his ways; the page sets it beside the senses plant and barren
the cane used for caning as a punishment of a court, a kind of <ciangduai>, rod
the book gives it as the opposite of <tukalh>, clash or be at odds: apparently agree, fit together
